abstract: BACKGROUND: Maspin is a tumor suppressor gene whose expression is altered in neoplasia and malignancies of many tissues. In the human placenta, the maspin gene is expressed in trophoblastic cells and might act as an inhibitory regulator of trophoblastic invasion. Hence, in gestational trophoblastic disease (GTD), where there is increased propensity for invasion in the trophoblastic tissue, we hypothesized that maspin expression would be decreased. The present study aimed at investigating the expression of maspin in GTD and its prognostic significance. METHODS: Using immunohistochemical staining, we firstly studied the expression of maspin in hydatidiform moles, with gestational age-matched normal first trimester placenta used as control. A total of 38 cases of hydatidiform moles were studied, including 20 complete moles (CM) and 18 partial moles (PM). Among them, 10 cases of the CM group and 8 cases of the PM group subsequently developed gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN). Immunostaining was also performed on tissue from 4 cases of choriocarcinoma and 5 cases of placental site trophoblastic tumor. Reverse transcriptase-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) was further performed on RNA extracted from 10 hydatidiform moles (5 with GTN and 5 without) and 6 normal first-trimester placentae. RESULTS: In all tissue sections, nuclear expression of immunostaining signal was demonstrated, mainly in the cytotrophoblasts. The percentage of trophoblastic nuclei stained in both complete and partial moles was significantly lower than that in normal first-trimester placenta (P < 0.001). However, there was no significant difference in immunostaining between complete and partial moles (P > 0.05). There was also significantly lower expression of maspin in those cases subsequently developing GTN than those which did not (P = 0.01). Immunostaining on choriocarcinoma and placental site trophoblastic tumor showed reduced expression of maspin in all the tumor cells. Reverse transcriptase-polymerase chain reaction revealed that the expression of maspin was consistently down-regulated in all the hydatidiform mole samples. CONCLUSIONS: Our results suggest that there is down-regulated expression of maspin in gestational trophoblastic diseases, and the down-regulation is more prominent in cases developing gestational trophoblastic neoplasia. This may play a role with prognostic significance in the pathogenesis and malignant transformation of hydatidiform moles.
abstract_ja: 背景：マスピンは多くの組織の腫瘍形成や悪性腫瘍で発現が変化する腫瘍抑制遺伝子です。ヒト胎盤では栄養膜細胞に発現し、栄養膜の浸潤を抑制する調節因子として働く可能性があります。妊娠性絨毛性疾患（GTD）は栄養膜組織の浸潤性が亢進しているため、マスピン発現は低下していると仮説を立てました。本研究では、GTDにおけるマスピン発現とその予後的意義を検討しました。方法：免疫組織化学染色により、胞状奇胎38例（完全奇胎20例、部分奇胎18例）のマスピン発現を検討し、妊娠週数を一致させた正常妊娠初期胎盤を対照としました。このうち完全奇胎10例と部分奇胎8例は、その後妊娠性絨毛性腫瘍（GTN）を発症しました。絨毛癌4例と胎盤部トロホブラスト腫瘍5例にも免疫染色を行いました。GTNを発症した5例とGTNを発症しなかった5例の胞状奇胎、および正常妊娠初期胎盤6例から抽出したRNAに逆転写ポリメラーゼ連鎖反応（RT-PCR）を行いました。結果：全切片で核の発現シグナルが認められ、主に細胞性栄養膜細胞に見られました。完全奇胎と部分奇胎のいずれも、トロホブラスト核の染色率は正常妊娠初期胎盤より有意に低値でした（P < 0.001）。完全奇胎と部分奇胎の間には有意差はありませんでした（P > 0.05）。その後GTNを発症した症例では、発症しなかった症例より有意にマスピン発現が低値でした（P = 0.01）。絨毛癌と胎盤部トロホブラスト腫瘍では、すべての腫瘍細胞で発現低下が認められました。RT-PCRでは、すべての胞状奇胎検体でマスピン発現が一貫して低下していました。結論：妊娠性絨毛性疾患ではマスピン発現が低下しており、GTNを発症する症例でその低下がより顕著でした。これは胞状奇胎の発症機序と悪性転化における予後的意義を持つ可能性があります。
